# Changelog

## 1.3.2

**New features**

- Added `AdsManager` with Unity Ads Legacy 4.16.4 as its built-in provider for async initialization and interstitial, rewarded, and banner loading/showing.
- Rewards are granted only when `AdsShowResult.ShouldGrantReward` is true.
- Added public `IAdsProvider` support for Unity LevelPlay, AppLovin MAX, Google AdMob/Google Ad Manager, FairBid, and other mediation SDKs.
- Added the `com.unity.ads` 4.16.4 dependency and automatic `AdsManager` registration in `AchManagerInstaller`.

**Documentation**

- Added synchronized four-language `AdsManager` setup and mediation migration guides.

## 1.3.1

**Changed**

- `IAPManager` explicitly uses Unity IAP Fake Store in the Unity Editor.
- Fake Store orders are automatically confirmed in the Editor when no `ReceiptValidator` or `PurchaseProcessor` is configured, allowing purchase UI flow tests without a backend.
- The Full Sample purchase popup enables Editor Fake Store testing without a validator. Real builds still require fulfillment validation.

## 1.3.0

**New features**

- Added the Unity 6000.3+ `AchEngine/Scene Navigator` toolbar. It lists Build Settings scenes, shows the active edit scene, and checks for unsaved changes before opening another scene.
- `UIRoot` now applies `UISafeAreaFitter` automatically to the `Screen`, `Popup`, and `Tooltip` layers. `Background` and `Overlay` remain full-screen layers.

**Improvements**

- Addressables asset and location caches now verify the requested type before reusing a handle.
- Temporary Addressables handles used for initialization, download-size checks, dependency downloads, catalog checks, and catalog updates are released automatically.
- Prevented duplicate debug-console callbacks when re-entering Play Mode with Domain Reload disabled.
- Updated runtime discovery to `FindFirstObjectByType` and avoided duplicate `DontDestroyOnLoad` calls for child UI roots.
- `IScene` is now an optional scene lifecycle hook; scenes that do not implement it no longer produce warnings.

**Documentation**

- Updated the Addressables, UI safe-area, Scene Navigator, and AI Assistant skill guides.
- Added the 1.2.0 and 1.3.0 release notes to the documentation site.

## 1.2.0

- Reworked Addressables around the static `AddressableManager` and `AchTask`-based asset, scene, instantiation, release, remote-download, and catalog APIs.
- Added location metadata and asset-handle caches, explicit scene-handle tracking, Addressables editor settings, watched-folder tooling, and updated samples.
- Updated the Addressables and integration guides for the explicit cache-release flow.

## 1.1.2

- Removed the iOS native debug console. The Android overlay and Editor IMGUI overlay remain available.

## 1.1.1

- Added the `IIAPReceiptValidator` extension point, Apple StoreKit 2 JWS/app-account-token support, manual restoration, and pending-fulfillment retry APIs.
- Added transaction-ID matching so a pending order cannot complete a different request for the same product.
- Added IAP unit tests and updated the Full Sample purchase documentation.

## 1.1.0

- Added Unity IAP 5.4.1 support through `IAPManager` and declared `com.unity.purchasing` as a package dependency.

## 1.0.8

- Added the `AIAssistantSkills/` definitions shipped with AchEngine.

## 1.0.7

- Fixed Addressables editor compilation when `com.unity.addressables` is not installed.
- Added the missing `AGENTS.md.meta` file.

## 1.0.6

- Removed the `AchEngine.Extensions` assembly and its extension-method guides.

## 1.0.5

- Added `AchTask` / `AchTask<T>` and the Korean and English async guides.

## 1.0.4

- Replaced `SoundManager` with `AudioManager`.
- Added `AudioManager`, `AchTimer`, `UIAchTimer`, button cooldown/hold helpers, `AchDebugConsole`, and RedDot reset/click-clear APIs.
- Updated all guides for the current API signatures and added documentation for the new features.

## 1.0.3

- Added save services, `AchProjectile`, standalone `AchFollower`, and multilingual TMP font baking.

## 1.0.2

- Added ECS, manager, singleton, logging, web-request, player-data, QuickSave, A\* pathfinding, AchMover, RedDot, UI, and Full Sample support.
- Improved Addressables, DI, Localization, Table, UI, and documentation coverage.

## 1.0.1

- Added JSON-to-CSV export tools for individual files and folders.

# Getting Started

A guide to experiencing AchEngine's core features in 5 minutes.

## 1. Set up the DI scope

Create an empty GameObject in the scene and add the `AchEngineScope` component.

```
Hierarchy
└── [AchEngineScope]   ← add the AchEngineScope component
```

## 2. Write an Installer

```csharp
using AchEngine.DI;
using UnityEngine;

public class GameInstaller : AchEngineInstaller
{
    public override void Install(IServiceBuilder builder)
    {
        builder
            .Register<IGameService, GameService>()
            .Register<IPlayerService, PlayerService>(ServiceLifetime.Transient);
    }
}
```

Drag `GameInstaller` into the **Installers** array of the `AchEngineScope` Inspector.

## 3. Create a UI Root

Click the **Create UI Root** button in **Project Settings › AchEngine › UI Workspace**, or place a `UIRoot` prefab in the scene.

## 4. Define a UIView

```csharp
using AchEngine.UI;

public class MainMenuView : UIView
{
    protected override void OnInitialize()
    {
        // called once on first creation
    }

    protected override void OnOpened()
    {
        // called when the transition completes after Show()
    }

    protected override void OnClosed()
    {
        // returned to the pool after Close()
    }
}
```

## 5. Show a View

```csharp
// Using [Inject] (requires VContainer)
[Inject] readonly IUIService _ui;
_ui.Show<MainMenuView>();

// Using ServiceLocator (for MonoBehaviours, etc.)
ServiceLocator.Resolve<IUIService>().Show("MainMenu");

// Close
_ui.Close<MainMenuView>();
```

## 6. Load table data

```csharp
// Type-safe access through TableManager
var itemTable = TableManager.Get<ItemTable>();
var sword = itemTable.Get(101);
Debug.Log(sword.Name); // "Iron Sword"
```

## Next steps

See the detailed description of each module in the left sidebar.

- [DI System](/AchEngine/en/usage/di.md)
- [UI System](/AchEngine/en/usage/ui.md)
- [Table Loader](/AchEngine/en/usage/table.md)
- [Addressables](/AchEngine/en/usage/addressables.md)
- [Localization](/AchEngine/en/usage/localization.md)
- [Module Integration Guide](/AchEngine/en/usage/integration.md)

# Introduction

AchEngine is an **integrated development toolkit** that bundles features you frequently use in Unity development into a single UPM package.

Each module can be used independently, and the core features keep working even without optional packages like VContainer, MemoryPack, or Addressables.

## Modules

| Module           | Description                                                | Optional package                   |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| **DI**           | VContainer wrapper, ServiceLocator                         | `jp.hadashikick.vcontainer`        |
| **UI System**    | Layer-based View management, pooling, transitions          | -                                  |
| **Table Loader** | Generates a C# data pipeline from Google Sheets            | `com.cysharp.memorypack`           |
| **Addressables** | Asset caching, automatic group management, remote delivery | `com.unity.addressables`           |
| **Localization** | JSON localization, key code generation                     | `com.unity.textmeshpro` (optional) |

## Package info

- **Package ID:** `com.achieve.engine`
- **Version:** 1.0.1
- **Minimum Unity version:** 6000.3
- **Required dependency:** `com.unity.ugui`

## Optional packages

Installing the packages below **automatically defines** the corresponding symbol and enables advanced AchEngine features. Not installing them causes no compile errors — only those features are disabled.

```
jp.hadashikick.vcontainer   -> enables DI container        -> ACHENGINE_VCONTAINER
com.cysharp.memorypack      -> enables binary serialization -> ACHENGINE_MEMORYPACK
com.unity.addressables      -> enables Addressables module  -> ACHENGINE_ADDRESSABLES
com.unity.textmeshpro       -> enables TMP Localization      -> ACHENGINE_LOCALIZATION_TMP
com.unity.entities          -> enables ECS wrapper           -> ACHENGINE_ENTITIES
```


> **Info**
> 
> You can check whether optional packages are installed at a glance in **Project Settings > AchEngine** Overview, and install them directly with a button.
>

# Watched Folders & Groups

Register a watched folder to add assets under that folder automatically to the selected Addressables group.

Open **Project Settings › AchEngine › Addressables › Watched Folders** and click **+ Add Folder**.

## Watched-folder fields

| Field                  | Description                                                            |
| ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Folder Path**        | A relative path beginning with `Assets/`, such as `Assets/Art/Icons`.  |
| **Group Name**         | The Addressables group name. It is created automatically when missing. |
| **Address Naming**     | File name, path relative to the watched folder, or the full path.      |
| **Include Subfolders** | Whether to scan child folders recursively.                             |
| **Labels**             | A comma-separated list of Addressables labels.                         |

## Address naming (`AddressNamingMode`)

| Value              | Example                                       |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------- |
| `FilenameOnly`     | `icon_sword`                                  |
| `RelativeToFolder` | `Icons/icon_sword` when watching `Assets/Art` |
| `FullPath`         | `Assets/Art/Icons/icon_sword`                 |

`FilenameOnly` can collide when different folders contain the same file name. Use `RelativeToFolder` when managing multiple folders.


> **Automatic scanning**
> 
> Unity's `AssetPostprocessor` updates watched folders when assets are added, moved, or deleted. Use **Rescan** or **AchEngine › Addressables › Re-scan Watched Folders** to register existing assets in one pass.
>

> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /AchEngine/en/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /AchEngine/en/llms-full.txt.

# Addressables — Overview

AchEngine's Addressables module wraps Unity Addressable Asset System and provides **location metadata caching**, **asset-handle caching**, and **automatic watched-folder grouping**. The static `AddressableManager` keeps initialization, loading, and releasing in one flow.


> **Optional module**
> 
> The module is enabled only when `com.unity.addressables` is installed. Install it from **Project Settings › AchEngine** Overview.
> 


## Core components

| Class                        | Role                                                       |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `AddressableManager`         | `AchTask`-based asset, scene, and remote-content APIs      |
| `AssetHandleCache`           | Caches loaded handles                                      |
| `LocationCache`              | Caches location metadata for addresses and labels          |
| `AddressableManagerSettings` | ScriptableObject for automatic Addressables initialization |

## Usage rules

- Async APIs return `AchTask` or `AchTask<T>` and can be awaited. They use UniTask when installed and `Task` otherwise.
- `LoadAsync` reuses a handle for the same address; `LoadAllAsync` reuses multi-load handles for the same label.
- Cached handles also verify the requested asset type. A handle for the same address or label is not reused for an incompatible type.
- The cache does not count references. Call `Release(key)` once when the owner no longer needs the asset.
- Release objects created by `InstantiateAsync` with `ReleaseInstance`; release the source prefab cache separately with `Release(address)`.
- Scenes are not unloaded automatically. Call `UnloadSceneAsync(address)` explicitly.

Temporary handles used by initialization, download-size checks, dependency downloads, catalog checks, and catalog updates are released automatically. Loaded assets and scenes still require an explicit `Release` or `UnloadSceneAsync`.

## Basic usage

```csharp
using AchEngine.Assets;

var sprite = await AddressableManager.LoadAsync<Sprite>("icon_sword");
spriteRenderer.sprite = sprite;

var icons = await AddressableManager.LoadAllAsync<Sprite>("ui-icons");

var hero = await AddressableManager.InstantiateAsync("Characters/Hero", transform);
AddressableManager.ReleaseInstance(hero);

AddressableManager.Release("icon_sword");
AddressableManager.Release("ui-icons");
AddressableManager.Release("Characters/Hero");
```

### Load and unload a scene

```csharp
await AddressableManager.LoadSceneAsync("Scenes/GameLevel");

// Release assets loaded separately by the scene before unloading it.
var unloaded = await AddressableManager.UnloadSceneAsync("Scenes/GameLevel");
```

`UnloadSceneAsync` only unloads scenes loaded through this API and returns `false` for unmanaged addresses.

### Download remote content

```csharp
await AddressableManager.DownloadDependenciesAsync(
    "remote_assets",
    progress => progressBar.value = progress.Percent);
```

## Clearing the cache

Release only the addresses owned by a screen or scene when its lifetime ends. For a full transition or logout, use `AddressableManager.ReleaseAll()` when it is safe to discard every cached asset.

## Next steps

- [Watched Folders & Groups](/AchEngine/en/usage/addressables/folders.md)
- [Remote Content](/AchEngine/en/usage/addressables/remote.md)

# Remote Content

## Configure remote content

The actual build and load paths for remote bundles are configured in Unity **Addressables Groups** Profiles and group schemas. Set the Build Path and Load Path of the remote groups to Remote, build the content, and deploy the generated files to that path.

Manage shared deployment information in **Project Settings › AchEngine › Addressables › Remote Content**.

| Field               | Description                                    |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| **Cloud Provider**  | AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, or Custom        |
| **Bucket / Region** | Values used to build the default S3 or GCS URL |
| **Catalog URL**     | A catalog URL that overrides the generated URL |
| **Bundle URL**      | A bundle URL that overrides the generated URL  |

## Recommended flow

1. Configure the remote groups and download labels in Unity Addressables.
2. Build with **AchEngine › Addressables › Build Content**.
3. Deploy the generated catalog and bundles to the remote Load Path.
4. At runtime, check the catalog and download dependencies for the labels you need.

## Check for catalog updates

```csharp
using AchEngine.Assets;

var catalogs = await AddressableManager.CheckForCatalogUpdatesAsync();
if (catalogs.Count > 0)
    await AddressableManager.UpdateCatalogsAsync(catalogs);
```

After a successful catalog update, the old location metadata cache is cleared automatically. Loaded asset caches remain; release changed addresses before loading them again.

Temporary handles used for initialization, download-size checks, dependency downloads, catalog checks, and updates are released when the operation ends. Explicitly release only assets that are no longer in use.

## Check size before downloading

```csharp
using AchEngine.Assets;

long size = await AddressableManager.GetDownloadSizeAsync("remote_assets");
if (size > 0)
{
    await AddressableManager.DownloadDependenciesAsync(
        "remote_assets",
        progress => progressBar.value = progress.Percent);
}
```

The return value is in bytes and excludes dependencies already in the cache.

## Build commands

Build content from **Project Settings › AchEngine › Addressables** or the **AchEngine › Addressables** menu.

| Command                     | Description                                             |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Build Content**           | Builds content with the current Addressables settings   |
| **Clean Build**             | Removes previous build output before rebuilding         |
| **Re-scan Watched Folders** | Scans watched folders and refreshes Addressable entries |


> **Use Fast Mode during development**
> 
> Set Play Mode to **Use Asset Database (Fast Mode)** during development to iterate without building bundles.
>

# AchTask

`AchTask` unifies UniTask and `System.Threading.Tasks.Task` behind one async API. When UniTask is installed the implementation uses UniTask; otherwise it falls back to `Task`.

## Package detection

When `com.cysharp.unitask` is present, the asmdef `versionDefines` automatically defines `ENABLE_UNITASK`.

| Environment       | Implementation                            |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| UniTask installed | `UniTask` / `UniTask<T>`                  |
| UniTask absent    | `System.Threading.Tasks.Task` / `Task<T>` |

## Await support

`AchTask` can be awaited directly.

```csharp
await AchTask.Delay(2f);
await AchTask.WaitUntil(() => isReady);
```

## Static factories

### `Delay` / `DelayRealtime`

```csharp
// Game-time delay (timeScale-aware with UniTask; wall-clock in the Task fallback).
await AchTask.Delay(1.5f);

// Real elapsed time, independent of timeScale.
await AchTask.DelayRealtime(1.5f);

var cts = new CancellationTokenSource();
await AchTask.Delay(5f, cts.Token);
```

Use `DelayRealtime` during slow motion when the wait should use real time.

### `WaitUntil`

```csharp
await AchTask.WaitUntil(() => player.IsGrounded);
await AchTask.WaitUntil(() => dialogueFinished, cts.Token);
```

### `WhenAll` / `WhenAny`

```csharp
var a = AchTask.Delay(1f);
var b = AchTask.Delay(2f);
var c = AchTask.Delay(3f);

await AchTask.WhenAll(a, b, c);
await AchTask.WhenAny(a, b, c);
```

### `CompletedTask`

```csharp
return condition ? DoWorkAsync() : AchTask.CompletedTask;
```

## Return values — `AchTask<T>`

```csharp
public static AchTask<string> FetchNameAsync()
    => AchTask<string>.FromResult("Player");

string name = await FetchNameAsync();
```

## Implicit conversions

```csharp
// UniTask environment
UniTask uniTask = someAchTask;
AchTask achTask = someUniTask;

// Task fallback environment
Task task = someAchTask.AsTask();
AchTask from = someTask;
```

## Complete example

```csharp
async AchTask LoadSequenceAsync(CancellationToken ct)
{
    await AchTask.Delay(0.5f, ct);
    await AchTask.WaitUntil(() => dataLoaded, ct);
    await AchTask.Delay(0.2f, ct);
}

async AchTask InitAllAsync()
{
    await AchTask.WhenAll(
        LoadAudioAsync(),
        LoadTableAsync(),
        LoadUserDataAsync());
}
```

## Related docs

- [AchTimer — progress-tracking timer](/AchEngine/en/usage/timer.md)
- [HttpLink — async HTTP requests](/AchEngine/en/usage/web-request.md)

# AchDebugConsole

`AchDebugConsole` is a debug console rendered in a native Android or iOS UI layer. It is independent of Unity's render thread and uses an IMGUI fallback in the Editor.

## Overview

It receives Unity `Log`, `Warning`, `Error`, `Exception`, and `Assert` messages through `Application.logMessageReceivedThreaded`. Registration happens automatically through `[RuntimeInitializeOnLoadMethod]`.

| Item                  | Value                                                       |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| Maximum retained logs | 500 (ring buffer)                                           |
| Colors                | Error/Exception/Assert → red, Warning → yellow, Log → white |
| Thread safety         | UI-thread dispatch on every platform                        |

## Platform behavior

### Android

The console is a floating `WindowManager` overlay. It can be dragged, uses 95% of the screen width and 50% of its height, and requires `SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW`.

### iOS

The console uses a separate `UIWindow` at `UIWindowLevelAlert + 100`. It is draggable, uses 95% of the width and 45% of the height, and requires no extra permission.

### Editor

`Show()` and `Hide()` only toggle internal state because the Editor already has a Console window. Use `DrawEditorGUI()` to show an overlay in the Game view.

## API

```csharp
public static class AchDebugConsole
{
    public static bool IsVisible { get; }
    public static void Show();
    public static void Hide();
    public static void Toggle();
    public static void Clear();
}
```

## Quick start

```csharp
using AchEngine;
using UnityEngine;

public class DebugConsoleTrigger : MonoBehaviour
{
    private void Update()
    {
        if (Input.touchCount != 4) return;

        bool allBegan = true;
        for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++)
        {
            if (Input.GetTouch(i).phase != TouchPhase.Began)
            {
                allBegan = false;
                break;
            }
        }

        if (allBegan)
            AchDebugConsole.Toggle();
    }
}
```

Attach the component to an empty GameObject. Replace the gesture with `Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.BackQuote)` for a keyboard shortcut.

## Editor fallback

```csharp
using AchEngine;
using UnityEngine;

public class AchDebugConsoleEditorOverlay : MonoBehaviour
{
#if UNITY_EDITOR
    private void OnGUI() => AchDebugConsole.DrawEditorGUI();
#endif
}
```


> **Android permission**
> 
> The package declares `SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW` through `AchDebugConsoleManifest.xml`. Android 6.0 (API 23) and later still require a runtime permission request before calling `Show()`.
> 



> **Performance**
> 
> Android and iOS render the console on their native UI threads, so keeping it open during profiling does not add work to Unity's main or render thread.
> 


## Related docs

# DI System — Overview

AchEngine provides a small DI abstraction without exposing VContainer directly.


> **Optional module**
> 
> The real DI container is enabled only when `jp.hadashikick.vcontainer` is installed. Without it, `ServiceLocator` remains usable with manual setup.
> 


## Core components

| Class                | Role                                                    |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `AchEngineScope`     | Scene entry point wrapping VContainer's `LifetimeScope` |
| `AchEngineInstaller` | Base class for defining service registrations           |
| `IServiceBuilder`    | Registration interface independent of VContainer        |
| `ServiceLocator`     | Static facade for resolving services at runtime         |

## Basic flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
A([Load scene]) --> B[AchEngineScope.Awake]
B --> C["AchEngineInstaller<br/>.Install(builder) × N"]
C --> D[("Build VContainer")]
D --> E[ServiceLocator.Setup]
E --> F{Runtime}
F --> G["[Inject]<br/>attribute injection"]
F --> H["ServiceLocator<br/>.Resolve<T>()"]
```

## `ServiceLifetime`

```csharp
public enum ServiceLifetime
{
    Singleton, // One instance per container (default)
    Transient, // A new instance per request
    Scoped,    // One instance per scope
}
```

## Next steps

- [AchEngineInstaller](/AchEngine/en/usage/di/installer.md)
- [ServiceLocator](/AchEngine/en/usage/di/locator.md)
- [DI lifecycle design](/AchEngine/en/usage/di/lifecycle.md)

# AchEngineInstaller

`AchEngineInstaller` defines service registrations for an `AchEngineScope`.

## `IServiceBuilder` API

```csharp
builder.Register<TService, TImplementation>();
builder.Register<TService, TImplementation>(ServiceLifetime.Singleton);
builder.Register<TService>();
builder.RegisterInstance<TService>(instance);
```

## 1. Write an installer

```csharp
using AchEngine.DI;

public class GameInstaller : AchEngineInstaller
{
    public override void Install(IServiceBuilder builder)
    {
        builder
            .Register<IGameService, GameService>()
            .Register<IPlayerService, PlayerService>(ServiceLifetime.Transient)
            .RegisterInstance<GameConfig>(config);
    }
}
```

## 2. Register it on `AchEngineScope`

Create an empty GameObject, add `AchEngineScope`, and add the `GameInstaller` component to its **Installers** array.

```text
AchEngineScope
└── Installers
    └── GameInstaller
```

## 3. Use services

### `[Inject]` (requires VContainer)

```csharp
public class GameController
{
    [Inject] private IGameService _game;
}
```

### `ServiceLocator` (available anywhere)

```csharp
var game = ServiceLocator.Resolve<IGameService>();
```

## Scope lifetime

`AchEngineScope` builds the container in `Awake` and disposes it in `OnDestroy`. A scope created in a scene therefore owns the services registered by that scene.


> **Relationship with ServiceLocator**
> 
> `ServiceLocator` points to the most recently initialized scope. When that scope is destroyed, the locator is cleared or replaced by the next active scope.
> 


```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant Scope as AchEngineScope
participant Installer as Installer
participant Container as DI Container
participant Locator as ServiceLocator
Scope->>Installer: Install(builder)
Installer->>Container: Register services
Scope->>Container: Build
Scope->>Locator: Setup(container)
Locator-->>Scope: Resolve services at runtime
Scope->>Container: Dispose on destroy
```


> **Multi-scene note**
> 
> Use one persistent scope for global services and separate additive scopes for scene-specific services. Do not replace a global scope accidentally when loading another scene.
>

url: /AchEngine/en/usage/di/lifecycle.md

> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /AchEngine/en/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /AchEngine/en/llms-full.txt.

# DI Lifecycle Design

This guide connects scene transitions, popups, data services, and in-game logic through DI.

## Overall structure

```mermaid
graph TB
subgraph Bootstrap["Bootstrap scene"]
AES[AchEngineScope]
UIR[UIRoot]
end
subgraph Lobby["Lobby scene (additive)"]
LS[LobbyScope]
LV[LobbyView]
end
subgraph InGame["InGame scene (additive)"]
GS[GameScope]
HV[HUDView]
end
Bootstrap --> Lobby
Bootstrap --> InGame
AES -.->|ServiceLocator| LS
AES -.->|ServiceLocator| GS
```

Register global services in Bootstrap and scene-specific services in the Lobby or InGame scopes. When a scene unloads, `AchEngineScope.OnDestroy()` disposes that scope's services.

## Scene transition

```csharp
public async Task LoadInGame(int stageId)
{
    ServiceLocator.Resolve<IUIService>().CloseAll();
    await SceneManager.UnloadSceneAsync("Lobby");
    await SceneManager.LoadSceneAsync("InGame", LoadSceneMode.Additive);
    ServiceLocator.Resolve<IGameService>().StartStage(stageId);
}
```

## Popup data

Pass data to a `UIView` popup through the `Show` callback:

```csharp
var ui = ServiceLocator.Resolve<IUIService>();
ui.Show<ItemDetailPopup>(popup => popup.SetItem(item, icon, iconAddress));
```

## Data services

Wrap Table data in a service and inject `ITableService` into game services. From a `MonoBehaviour`, use `ServiceLocator.Resolve<T>()` when container construction is not involved.

## Next steps

- [Module integration](/AchEngine/en/usage/integration.md)
- [AchEngineInstaller](/AchEngine/en/usage/di/installer.md)

url: /AchEngine/en/usage/di/locator.md

> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /AchEngine/en/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /AchEngine/en/llms-full.txt.

# ServiceLocator

> **VContainer-free use**
> 
> `ServiceLocator` can be initialized manually even when VContainer is not installed. With VContainer installed, `AchEngineScope` normally initializes it for you.
> 


## API

```csharp
ServiceLocator.Setup(IServiceProvider provider);
T service = ServiceLocator.Resolve<T>();
bool exists = ServiceLocator.TryResolve<T>(out var service);
ServiceLocator.Clear();
```

## Example

```csharp
public class EnemySpawner : MonoBehaviour
{
    private IEnemyService _enemies;

    private void Start()
    {
        _enemies = ServiceLocator.Resolve<IEnemyService>();
    }
}
```

## `[Inject]` vs `ServiceLocator`

Use `[Inject]` for objects created by the VContainer container. Use `ServiceLocator` from `MonoBehaviour`, static callbacks, or objects Unity creates directly.

## Manual initialization without VContainer

Register a provider or service collection during bootstrap, then call `ServiceLocator.Setup(...)` before any consumer resolves a service.


> **Non-VContainer environment**
> 
> `ServiceLocator` is a lookup facade, not a lifetime manager. The bootstrap code owns service creation and disposal when no DI container is present.
> 


## Related docs

- [DI system overview](/AchEngine/en/usage/di.md)
- [DI lifecycle design](/AchEngine/en/usage/di/lifecycle.md)

# ECS Wrapper

The ECS helpers connect Unity Entities with the AchEngine service and world abstractions. The module is optional and is compiled only when `com.unity.entities` is installed.

## Basic usage

```csharp
using AchEngine.ECS;
using Unity.Entities;

public partial struct DamageSystem : ISystem
{
    public void OnUpdate(ref SystemState state)
    {
        var ecb = state.World.GetOrCreateSystemManaged<EndSimulationEntityCommandBufferSystem>();
        // Query and update entities here.
    }
}
```

## When should I use it?

Use the wrapper when gameplay data is already modeled as Entities and you need consistent world access, command buffers, bakers, or DI integration. Keep ordinary UI and scene orchestration in the regular AchEngine modules.

## Use it from a system

```csharp
public partial struct SpawnSystem : ISystem
{
    public void OnCreate(ref SystemState state) { }

    public void OnUpdate(ref SystemState state)
    {
        var world = state.World;
        var entityManager = world.EntityManager;
        // entityManager.CreateEntity(...);
    }
}
```

## `EntityManager` extensions

The package provides convenience extensions for creating, querying, and retrieving components while keeping the standard `EntityManager` API available.

```csharp
var entity = entityManager.CreateEntity(archetype);
entityManager.SetComponentData(entity, new Health { Value = 100 });
```

## Use it from a Baker

```csharp
public class UnitAuthoring : MonoBehaviour
{
    public int health = 100;
}

public class UnitBaker : Baker<UnitAuthoring>
{
    public override void Bake(UnitAuthoring authoring)
    {
        var entity = GetEntity(TransformUsageFlags.Dynamic);
        AddComponent(entity, new Health { Value = authoring.health });
    }
}
```

## Inject an ECS world through DI

Register the desired world or an adapter in an installer and inject that abstraction into systems or services. This keeps world selection explicit in multi-world projects.

```csharp
builder.RegisterInstance(World.Default);
builder.Register<IWorldService, WorldService>();
```

# Installation

## UPM — install from a Git URL (recommended)

Open **Window › Package Manager** in the Unity Editor, choose **+ › Add package from git URL...**, and enter:

```
https://github.com/achieveonepark/AchEngine.git
```

Pin a specific version by adding a tag:

```
https://github.com/achieveonepark/AchEngine.git#1.0.0
```

## Install through `manifest.json`

Add the package directly to `Packages/manifest.json`:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "com.achieve.engine": "https://github.com/achieveonepark/AchEngine.git"
  }
}
```

## Optional packages

AchEngine supports the following optional packages. Installing one enables its feature automatically. Check the status in **Window › AchEngine › AchEngine Info**.

| Package      | Package ID                  | Enabled features                                  |
| ------------ | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| VContainer   | `jp.hadashikick.vcontainer` | DI container (`AchEngineScope`, `ServiceLocator`) |
| MemoryPack   | `com.cysharp.memorypack`    | QuickSave serialization (`USE_QUICK_SAVE`)        |
| Addressables | `com.unity.addressables`    | `AddressableManager`, remote content              |
| R3           | `com.cysharp.r3`            | `UIBindingManager` reactive pub/sub               |

### Install VContainer manually

Add the registry and dependency to `Packages/manifest.json`:

```json
{
  "scopedRegistries": [
    {
      "name": "package.openupm.com",
      "url": "https://package.openupm.com",
      "scopes": ["jp.hadashikick.vcontainer"]
    }
  ],
  "dependencies": {
    "jp.hadashikick.vcontainer": "1.15.0"
  }
}
```

For MemoryPack, see the [MemoryPack installation guide](https://github.com/Cysharp/MemoryPack). For R3, see the [R3 repository](https://github.com/Cysharp/R3).

## Verify the installation

The Unity Console should contain no package errors, and **Window › AchEngine › AchEngine Info** should be available. The window shows the package and feature status at a glance.

# Module Integration

This guide combines DI, Table Loader, Localization, Addressables, and UI into one gameplay flow.

## Overall structure

```mermaid
graph TB
subgraph Bootstrap["Bootstrap scene"]
GI[GlobalInstaller]
GI --> TS[ITableService]
GI --> UI[IUIService]
GI --> AU[IAudioService]
GI --> NW[INetworkService]
UIR[UIRoot]
end
subgraph Lobby["Lobby scene (additive)"]
LI[LobbyInstaller]
LI --> SH[IShopService]
LI --> FR[IFriendService]
end
subgraph InGame["InGame scene (additive)"]
GAI[GameInstaller]
GAI --> GM[IGameService]
GAI --> ST[IStageService]
GAI --> ES[IEnemySpawner]
end
Bootstrap --> Lobby
Bootstrap --> InGame
```

## Table Loader + Localization

Store localization keys in the table instead of translated text:

```text
| Id  | NameKey           | DescKey           | Price |
|-----|-------------------|-------------------|-------|
| 101 | item.sword.name   | item.sword.desc   | 500   |
| 102 | item.wand.name    | item.wand.desc    | 1200  |
```

```csharp
public void SetItem(int itemId)
{
    var item = TableManager.Get<ItemTable>().Get(itemId);
    _nameText.text = LocalizationManager.Get(item.NameKey);
    _descText.text = LocalizationManager.Get(item.DescKey);
    _priceText.text = $"{item.Price:N0} G";
}
```

After key generation, use `L.Item.Sword.Name` for fixed keys or keep the table key for dynamic content.

## Table Loader + Addressables

Store `IconAddress` and `SfxAddress` in the table, load the asset when the view opens, and release it when the view closes.

```csharp
private string _loadedAddress;

public async void SetItem(int itemId)
{
    var item = TableManager.Get<ItemTable>().Get(itemId);
    if (_loadedAddress != null)
        AddressableManager.Release(_loadedAddress);

    _loadedAddress = item.IconAddress;
    _iconImage.sprite = await AddressableManager.LoadAsync<Sprite>(_loadedAddress);
}

protected override void OnClosed()
{
    if (_loadedAddress == null) return;
    AddressableManager.Release(_loadedAddress);
    _loadedAddress = null;
}
```

## Three-module example

When opening an item popup, read the table row, resolve localized text, and load the icon asynchronously:

```csharp
public async void SetItem(int itemId)
{
    var item = TableManager.Get<ItemTable>().Get(itemId);
    _nameText.text = LocalizationManager.Get(item.NameKey);
    _descText.text = LocalizationManager.Get(item.DescKey);
    _iconImage.sprite = await AddressableManager.LoadAsync<Sprite>(item.IconAddress);
}
```

## DI service layer

Wrap static managers behind an interface when a service needs to be unit-tested:

```csharp
public interface IItemService
{
    ItemData GetItem(int id);
    string GetItemName(int id);
}

public class ItemService : IItemService
{
    private readonly ITableService _tables;
    private readonly ILocalizationService _localization;

    public ItemService(ITableService tables, ILocalizationService localization)
    {
        _tables = tables;
        _localization = localization;
    }

    public ItemData GetItem(int id) => _tables.Get<ItemTable>().Get(id);
    public string GetItemName(int id) => _localization.Get(GetItem(id).NameKey);
}
```

Register `ITableService`, `ILocalizationService`, and `IItemService` in the global installer, then inject `IItemService` into views or game services.

## Scene transition + UI flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
participant App as App start
participant Boot as Bootstrap scene
participant SL as ServiceLocator
participant SS as SceneService
participant GS as GameService
participant UI as IUIService
participant TBL as TableManager
participant LOC as LocalizationManager
participant ADDR as AddressableManager
App->>Boot: Load scene
Boot->>SL: Setup global services
SS->>UI: CloseAll()
SS->>Boot: Unload Lobby
SS->>Boot: Load InGame
SS->>GS: StartStage(stageId)
GS->>TBL: Get stage data
GS->>UI: Show<GameHUDView>()
UI->>TBL: Get item data
TBL-->>UI: ItemData
UI->>LOC: Get(NameKey)
UI->>ADDR: LoadAsync<Sprite>(IconAddress)
```

# Key Constant Code Generation

The Localization editor can generate a nested static class from dot-separated keys.

## Conversion example

```json
{
  "menu.start": "Start",
  "item.sword.name": "Iron Sword"
}
```

```csharp
L.Menu.Start
L.Item.Sword.Name
```

The generated constants are ordinary strings, so they can be passed directly to `LocalizationManager.Get`.

## Code-generation settings

Configure the following fields on `LocalizationSettings`:

| Field                 | Description                          |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `generatedClassName`  | Root class name; defaults to `L`     |
| `generatedNamespace`  | Optional namespace                   |
| `generatedOutputPath` | C# output path                       |
| Database              | Locale database used to collect keys |

Run **AchEngine › Localization › Generate Key Class** after changing the database.

## `LocalizedString`

Use `LocalizedString` when a field should expose a key dropdown in the Inspector.

```csharp
[LocalizedString]
[SerializeField] private LocalizedString _title;

private void Refresh()
{
    titleText.text = _title.Value;
}
```



---
url: /AchEngine/en/usage/localization/index.md

> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /AchEngine/en/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /AchEngine/en/llms-full.txt.

# Localization — Overview

AchEngine Localization loads JSON locale files, resolves keys at runtime, and can generate type-safe key constants.

## Core components

| Type                   | Role                                             |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `LocalizationManager`  | Static runtime API for lookup and locale changes |
| `LocalizationSettings` | Default/fallback locale and database settings    |
| `LocaleDatabase`       | Maps locales to JSON `TextAsset` files           |
| `LocalizedString`      | Inspector-friendly key field                     |
| `LocalizedText`        | Refreshes `Text` or `TMP_Text` automatically     |

## Basic usage

```csharp
string title = LocalizationManager.Get("menu.title");
string welcome = LocalizationManager.Get("dialog.welcome", "Player1", 5);

LocalizationManager.LocaleChanged += OnLocaleChanged;
LocalizationManager.SetLocale("ja");
```

## JSON format

```json
{
  "menu.title": "Settings",
  "dialog.welcome": "Welcome, {0}!"
}
```

Nested keys are supported when the code-generation option is enabled:

```json
{
  "menu": {
    "start": "Start",
    "quit": "Quit"
  }
}
```

## Automatic TMP refresh

Add `LocalizedText` to a `Text` or `TMP_Text`, choose a key, and it will refresh when `LocalizationManager.LocaleChanged` fires.


> **TMP support**
> 
> TMP support requires the `ACHENGINE_LOCALIZATION_TMP` scripting symbol. It is automatically defined when `com.unity.textmeshpro` is installed.
> 


## FontAsset Maker

Use **AchEngine › Localization › FontAsset Maker** to collect the characters used by the locale files and create a separate TMP FontAsset for each language.

## Next steps

- [Settings & database](/AchEngine/en/usage/localization/setup.md)
- [Key constant code generation](/AchEngine/en/usage/localization/codegen.md)



---
url: /AchEngine/en/usage/localization/setup.md
---

> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /AchEngine/en/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /AchEngine/en/llms-full.txt.

# Settings & Database

## 1. Create `LocalizationSettings`

Create the asset from **Create › Achieve › Localization › Settings** and place it at `Resources/LocalizationSettings`.

## 2. Create a `LocaleDatabase`

Create **Create › Achieve › Localization › Locale Database**, then add one locale and JSON `TextAsset` pair for each language.

## 3. Add JSON files

```json
{
  "menu.start": "Start",
  "menu.quit": "Quit"
}
```

```json
{
  "menu.start": "開始",
  "menu.quit": "終了"
}
```

Keep keys identical across locale files. Only the values should change.

## 4. Configure locales

Set `defaultLocaleCode`, `fallbackLocaleCode`, `autoDetectSystemLanguage`, `autoInitialize`, and the `database` field on `LocalizationSettings`.

## Runtime initialization

Automatic initialization runs before the first scene when `autoInitialize` is enabled and the settings asset contains a database. Manual initialization is also available:

```csharp
LocalizationManager.Initialize();
LocalizationManager.SetLocale("en");
```

## Editor window

Open **AchEngine › Localization › Localization Table** to inspect and edit keys, import CSV/JSON, and verify that locale files contain the same key set.

> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /AchEngine/en/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /AchEngine/en/llms-full.txt.

# AdsManager

`AdsManager` uses Unity Ads Legacy 4.16.4 as its default provider for interstitial,
rewarded, and banner ads. `com.unity.ads` is an AchEngine 1.3.2 dependency, so Unity's
Package Manager resolves it with the package. `AchManagerInstaller` registers `AdsManager`.

Live ads require the Android/iOS game IDs and ad-unit IDs from Unity Dashboard. The Editor
uses the Android game ID; configure it as well. Keep `testMode` enabled only during development.

## Quick setup

Configure the manager once before initialization in your bootstrap. With VContainer, apply the
same calls to an injected `AdsManager`.

```csharp
var ads = ServiceLocator.Resolve<AdsManager>();

ads.Configure(new AdsConfiguration(
    androidGameId: "Android game ID",
    iosGameId: "iOS game ID",
    interstitialAdUnitId: "Interstitial_Android",
    rewardedAdUnitId: "Rewarded_Android",
    bannerAdUnitId: "Banner_Android",
    testMode: true));

ads.InitializationFailed += message => Debug.LogError(message);

await ads.Initialize();
await ads.LoadInterstitialAsync();
await ads.LoadRewardedAsync();
```

If Android and iOS use different ad-unit IDs, create the appropriate `AdsConfiguration` in each
platform bootstrap. `Configure()` can only run before initialization begins.

## Interstitial and rewarded ads

Load an ad before showing it, then reload every fullscreen ad after a show attempt. Grant a
reward only when `ShouldGrantReward` is true; skipped or failed rewarded ads must grant nothing.

```csharp
var result = await ads.ShowRewardedAsync();

if (result.ShouldGrantReward)
    GrantCoinsToPlayer();
else if (!result.IsSuccess)
    Debug.LogWarning(result.Message);

await ads.LoadRewardedAsync();
```

## Banner ads

The Unity Ads provider shows banners at bottom center. A successful `ShowBannerAsync()` means
the request reached the SDK, not that it produced an impression.

```csharp
await ads.LoadBannerAsync();
await ads.ShowBannerAsync();
ads.HideBanner();
```

## Mediation

The default provider is a small Unity Ads Legacy integration. For new live operations and
competition among multiple networks, use one of these mediation products:

| Option                              | Best fit                                                          | AchEngine integration                                                           |
| ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Unity LevelPlay                     | Unity Ads-centered operations and Unity's current mediation stack | Wrap the LevelPlay SDK in `IAdsProvider`.                                       |
| AppLovin MAX                        | Advanced monetization/bidding tools and broad network operations  | Implement a MAX Unity SDK `IAdsProvider`.                                       |
| Google AdMob / Google Ad Manager    | Existing Google ads, Firebase, or GAM reporting stack             | Wrap the AdMob Unity SDK and its currently supported Unity Ads network adapter. |
| Digital Turbine FairBid and similar | Existing agreement or tooling with that provider                  | Wrap that provider's Unity SDK in the same interface.                           |

Adapter availability, bidding support, minimum Android/iOS SDK versions, and privacy/ATT
requirements change frequently. Before integrating, confirm the selected mediator's current
Unity Ads adapter and platform requirements.

```csharp
// Replace the default provider with an adapter around a mediation SDK.
var ads = AdsManager.Create(new MyLevelPlayAdsProvider());
```

`IAdsProvider` contains only initialization, load/show, and banner-hide operations. The adapter
must map its callbacks to `AdsLoadResult`/`AdsShowResult` and return `Completed` only after a
rewarded ad finishes. Do not initialize a Legacy Unity Ads provider and LevelPlay together in
the same app session.

## API

| Member                                                                  | Description                                                |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Configure(configuration)`                                              | Sets game IDs and ad-unit IDs before initialization.       |
| `Initialize()`                                                          | Initializes the provider with the active platform game ID. |
| `LoadInterstitialAsync()` / `LoadRewardedAsync()` / `LoadBannerAsync()` | Loads an ad for display.                                   |
| `ShowInterstitialAsync()` / `ShowRewardedAsync()` / `ShowBannerAsync()` | Shows a loaded ad and returns its result.                  |
| `HideBanner()`                                                          | Hides the active banner.                                   |
| `IsLoaded(placement)`                                                   | Checks display readiness for an ad placement.              |
| `AdsShowResult.ShouldGrantReward`                                       | True only for a completed rewarded ad.                     |

url: /AchEngine/en/usage/managers/audio.md
---

> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /AchEngine/en/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /AchEngine/en/llms-full.txt.

# AudioManager

`AudioManager` handles BGM, SFX, fades, mute state, and spatial audio. It replaces the removed `SoundManager`.

## DI registration

Register it through `AchManagerInstaller` or directly:

```csharp
builder.Register<AudioManager>();
```

Resolve it with:

```csharp
var audio = ServiceLocator.Resolve<AudioManager>();
```

## API

| Member                                        | Description                                     |
| --------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `BgmVolume`                                   | BGM volume from 0 to 1                          |
| `SfxVolume`                                   | SFX volume from 0 to 1                          |
| `PlayBgm(clip)`                               | Plays immediately; ignores the same active clip |
| `PlayBgm(clip, fadeDuration)`                 | Crossfades to a new BGM                         |
| `StopBgm()` / `StopBgm(fadeDuration)`         | Stops immediately or after a fade               |
| `SetBgmVolume(volume, fadeDuration)`          | Changes BGM volume over time                    |
| `MuteBgm(bool)`                               | Mutes/restores BGM output                       |
| `MuteSfx(bool)`                               | Mutes/restores SFX output                       |
| `MuteAll(bool)`                               | Mutes/restores both channels                    |
| `PlaySfx(clip)`                               | Plays a 2D SFX                                  |
| `PlaySfxAt(clip, worldPosition, volumeScale)` | Plays a 3D SFX at a world position              |

## SFX channel pool

SFX uses an internal pool of eight `AudioSource` channels. It prefers a free channel and overwrites the oldest channel in round-robin order when all channels are busy. The pool survives scene changes through `DontDestroyOnLoad`.

## Mute behavior

Mute changes the actual output to zero without changing `BgmVolume` or `SfxVolume`, so unmuting restores the previous volume.

```csharp
audio.BgmVolume = 0.8f;
audio.MuteBgm(true);   // Output: 0, stored volume: 0.8
audio.MuteBgm(false);  // Output: 0.8
```

## Examples

```csharp
var audio = ServiceLocator.Resolve<AudioManager>();
audio.PlayBgm(lobbyBgmClip, fadeDuration: 1f);
audio.SetBgmVolume(0.3f, fadeDuration: 2f);
audio.PlaySfxAt(explosionClip, explosionObject.transform.position);
audio.PlaySfx(buttonClickClip);
audio.MuteAll(false);
```

url: /AchEngine/en/usage/managers/config.md

> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /AchEngine/en/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /AchEngine/en/llms-full.txt.

# ConfigManager

`ConfigManager` is a PlayerPrefs-based key-value store for simple options such as volume and language.

## API

```csharp
var cfg = ServiceLocator.Resolve<ConfigManager>();

cfg.AddKey("bgmVolume", 1.0f);
cfg.AddKey("language", "en");

float volume = cfg.GetConfig<float>("bgmVolume", fallback: 1f);
cfg.SetConfig("bgmVolume", 0.5f);
```

`SetConfig` does nothing for a key that has not been registered with `AddKey`.

url: /AchEngine/en/usage/managers/iap.md

> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /AchEngine/en/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /AchEngine/en/llms-full.txt.

# IAPManager

`IAPManager` uses Unity IAP 5.4.1 `StoreController` APIs for store connection, product lookup, purchase, pending-order retry, and restoration. In player builds, it confirms an order only after its reward has been persisted.

`com.unity.purchasing` 5.4.1 is an AchEngine dependency, and `AchManagerInstaller` registers `IAPManager` automatically.

## Quick setup

Product IDs must exactly match Google Play Console or App Store Connect. For player builds, configure products and a receipt validator before initialization.

```csharp
var iap = ServiceLocator.Resolve<IAPManager>();

iap.AddProduct("com.mygame.coins_100", ProductType.Consumable);
iap.AddProduct("com.mygame.remove_ads", ProductType.NonConsumable);
iap.ReceiptValidator = new GameReceiptValidator();

await iap.Initialize();
```

## Editor Fake Store testing

In the Unity Editor, `IAPManager` explicitly selects Unity IAP's `fake` store.
Only in the Editor, a Fake Store order is automatically confirmed when both
`ReceiptValidator` and `PurchaseProcessor` are unset. This lets you test purchase
buttons, completion events, and popup flow without making a real payment or
calling a backend.

This behavior is compiled only under `UNITY_EDITOR`. Android, iOS, and other
player builds still require a receipt validator or fulfillment processor before
a purchase can start. The editor fake order is not granted as a real purchase.

The Full Sample `PurchasePopup` also enables its purchase buttons without a
validator in the Editor. Assign the game-specific server validator to the
`Receipt Validator` field for real builds.

Implement `IIAPReceiptValidator` in the game project. Authenticate the player, send platform transaction data to the backend, and persist rewards idempotently on the server.

```csharp
public sealed class GameReceiptValidator : IIAPReceiptValidator
{
    public async Task<IAPReceiptValidationResult> ValidateAndFulfillAsync(IAPPurchase purchase)
    {
        var response = await SendToGameServerAsync(purchase);
        return response.IsSuccess
            ? IAPReceiptValidationResult.Succeeded()
            : IAPReceiptValidationResult.Failed(response.Message);
    }
}
```

## Purchase requests

`PurchaseAsync` returns only after store purchase, server fulfillment, and order confirmation are complete. In player builds, without a validator or processor, it does not open the purchase dialog. The Editor uses the Fake Store flow described above.

```csharp
var result = await iap.PurchaseAsync("com.mygame.coins_100");
if (result.IsSuccess)
    Debug.Log("Purchase and fulfillment confirmed.");
else
    Debug.LogWarning($"Purchase state: {result.Status}, {result.Message}");
```

| Status               | Meaning                                                            |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Confirmed`          | Receipt validated, reward persisted, and store order confirmed     |
| `Failed`             | User canceled or the store purchase failed                         |
| `Deferred`           | Purchase is waiting for approval                                   |
| `PendingFulfillment` | Validation or reward persistence failed; order remains unconfirmed |

## Server receipt validation

Send the transaction ID, Unity receipt, Apple StoreKit 2 JWS, app-account token, and product list to the server. The server should use the transaction ID as an idempotency key and return matching `transactionId`, `isValid`, and `isFulfilled` values.

```json
{
  "transactionId": "store transaction ID",
  "receipt": "Unity IAP receipt",
  "appleJwsRepresentation": "StoreKit 2 JWS or empty string",
  "appleAppAccountToken": "app account token or empty string",
  "products": [{ "productId": "com.mygame.coins_100", "productType": "Consumable", "quantity": 1 }]
}
```

Retry unfulfilled orders in the current session or re-read the store purchase list:

```csharp
await iap.RetryPendingFulfillmentsAsync();
await iap.GetPendingListAsync();
```

## Restore and events

`Initialize()` reads existing purchases after product discovery. Update non-consumable and subscription ownership from `PurchaseRestored`. Apple apps should expose a user-facing restore button:

```csharp
iap.PurchaseRestored += purchase =>
{
    foreach (var item in purchase.Items)
        Debug.Log($"Restored: {item.ProductId}");
};

var restore = await iap.RestoreTransactionsAsync();
```

## API

| Member                            | Description                                              |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `AddProduct(id, type)`            | Registers a product before initialization                |
| `ReceiptValidator`                | Server validator and idempotent fulfillment hook         |
| `PurchaseProcessor`               | Custom async processor when no server validator is used  |
| `Initialize()`                    | Connects, fetches products, and reads existing purchases |
| `PurchaseAsync(id)`               | Starts a purchase and returns `IAPPurchaseResult`        |
| `RetryPendingFulfillmentsAsync()` | Retries pending orders held in the current session       |
| `GetPendingListAsync()`           | Reads existing purchases and retries pending orders      |
| `RestoreTransactionsAsync()`      | Starts the Apple manual-restore flow                     |
| `TryGetProduct(id, out product)`  | Retrieves a fetched Unity IAP `Product`                  |

Always make fulfillment idempotent by transaction ID. A validator or processor failure leaves the order unconfirmed so it can be retried.

url: /AchEngine/en/usage/managers/index.md
---

> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /AchEngine/en/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /AchEngine/en/llms-full.txt.

# Manager System

AchEngine managers register common game services through DI and make them available through `ServiceLocator`.

## Available managers

| Manager           | Role                                           |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `ConfigManager`   | PlayerPrefs-based settings                     |
| `AudioManager`    | BGM/SFX, fades, mute, and 3D audio             |
| `AchSceneManager` | Async scene transitions and `IScene` lifecycle |
| `InputManager`    | Input enable/disable wrapper                   |
| `TimeManager`     | Network time and one-second events             |
| `PoolManager`     | Prefab-based object pooling                    |
| `PlayerManager`   | Typed player-data containers                   |
| `SaveManager`     | Save/load/delete through `ISaveService`        |
| `IAPManager`      | Unity IAP 5.4.1 purchase and receipt flow      |

## Quick start

### 1. Add `AchManagerInstaller`

Add the `AchManagerInstaller` component to the Installers array of `AchEngineScope`.

```csharp
// All built-in managers are registered as singletons.
```

To register only selected managers, derive from it:

```csharp
public class MyInstaller : AchManagerInstaller
{
    public override void Install(IServiceBuilder builder)
    {
        builder
            .Register<ConfigManager>()
            .Register<AudioManager>();
    }
}
```

### 2. Resolve a manager

```csharp
using AchEngine.DI;
using AchEngine.Managers;

var config = ServiceLocator.Resolve<ConfigManager>();
var audio = ServiceLocator.Resolve<AudioManager>();
```

## `IScene` lifecycle

Add a MonoBehaviour implementing `IScene` to a scene root. `AchSceneManager` calls `OnSceneStart` and `OnSceneEnd` during transitions.

```csharp
public class LobbyScene : MonoBehaviour, IScene
{
    public async Task OnSceneStart() => await LoadUserDataAsync();
    public Task OnSceneEnd() => Task.CompletedTask;
}
```

Runtime async APIs use `System.Threading.Tasks.Task`.

> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /AchEngine/en/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /AchEngine/en/llms-full.txt.

# PlayerManager & Player Data

`PlayerManager` stores `PlayerDataContainerBase<TKey, TValue>` containers by type.

## Create a container

```csharp
public class InventoryContainer : PlayerDataContainerBase<int, ItemData>
{
    public InventoryContainer()
    {
        DataKey = nameof(InventoryContainer);
        _dataDic = new Dictionary<int, ItemData>();
    }
}
```

## Register and access

```csharp
var player = ServiceLocator.Resolve<PlayerManager>();
player.AddContainer(new InventoryContainer());

var inventory = player.GetContainer<InventoryContainer>();
inventory.Add(101, new ItemData { Id = 101, Name = "Sword" });
var sword = inventory.GetInfo(101);

player.RemoveContainer<InventoryContainer>();
```

## `PlayerDataBase`

The base class for an individual data item contains an `int Id` field.

```csharp
public class ItemData : PlayerDataBase
{
    public string Name;
    public int Quantity;
}
```

## `PlayerData`

```csharp
var data = new PlayerData { Id = 1, Name = "Hero", Level = 10 };
```

## Save and load

Persistence is owned by `SaveManager`, not `PlayerManager`. See [SaveManager](/AchEngine/en/usage/managers/save.md).

# PoolManager

`PoolManager` wraps Unity `ObjectPool<GameObject>` to reduce GC pressure from repeatedly created bullets, particles, and similar objects.

## API

```csharp
var pool = ServiceLocator.Resolve<PoolManager>();

pool.RegisterPool("Bullet", bulletPrefab, defaultCapacity: 20, maxSize: 100);

var bullet = pool.Get<BulletComponent>("Bullet");
var gameObject = pool.Get("Bullet");

pool.Release("Bullet", gameObject);
pool.ClearPool("Bullet");
pool.ClearAll();
```

url: /AchEngine/en/usage/managers/save.md

> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /AchEngine/en/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /AchEngine/en/llms-full.txt.

# SaveManager & Save System

`SaveManager` abstracts save, load, and delete behind `ISaveService`. Since it is separate from `PlayerManager`, a local file backend can later be replaced with Firestore, AWS, or Cloudflare D1 without changing game code.

## Structure

```text
SaveManager       ← injected through DI
  └─ ISaveService ← backend replacement point
       └─ LocalSaveService ← QuickSave local implementation
```

## Quick start

### 1. Register with DI

```csharp
builder.Register<PlayerManager>();
builder.Register<ISaveService, LocalSaveService>();
builder.Register<SaveManager>();
```

### 2. Configure

Call `Configure()` on `ISaveService` once before saving or loading:

```csharp
var saveService = ServiceLocator.Resolve<ISaveService>();
saveService.Configure(encryptionKey: "myKey12345678!", version: 1);

var save = ServiceLocator.Resolve<SaveManager>();
```

`encryptionKey` should be at least 16 characters. `version` supports data migrations.

## Synchronous API

```csharp
save.Save();
PlayerManager loaded = save.Load();
save.Delete();
```

## Async API

```csharp
await save.SaveAsync();
PlayerManager loaded = await save.LoadAsync();
await save.DeleteAsync();
```

## Check for a save file

```csharp
bool hasData = save.IsExist;
```

## Custom backend

Implement `ISaveService` and register it instead of `LocalSaveService`:

```csharp
builder.Register<ISaveService, FirestoreSaveService>();
```

## Editor menu (`USE_QUICK_SAVE`)

When QuickSave is installed, **Achieve › Delete Save** deletes `.acqs` save files in one action.

# AchSceneManager

`AchSceneManager` provides asynchronous scene transitions and manages scene lifecycle through `IScene`.

## Implement `IScene`

Attach an `IScene` component to a scene root:

```csharp
public class GameScene : MonoBehaviour, IScene
{
    public async Task OnSceneStart() { /* initialize */ }
    public Task OnSceneEnd() => Task.CompletedTask;
}
```

## API

```csharp
var scenes = ServiceLocator.Resolve<AchSceneManager>();

await scenes.LoadSceneAsync("Lobby");
await scenes.ReloadSceneAsync();
await scenes.UnloadSceneAsync("SubScene");

scenes.OnSceneLoadStarted += ShowLoadingUI;
AchSceneManager.OnSceneLoadCompleted += HideLoadingUI;
```

The `Ach` prefix distinguishes this manager from Unity's `UnityEngine.SceneManagement.SceneManager`.

# Unity MCP Skills — Overview

AchEngine ships Unity AI Assistant (MCP) skill definitions so the Assistant can use the package's existing systems instead of reimplementing them with raw Unity APIs.


> **What is Unity AI Assistant (MCP)?**
> 
> Unity AI Assistant can discover package-provided skills through MCP. A skill describes when and how to use a system and is not a runtime dependency of your game.
> 


## Where the skills live

```text
AchEngine/
└── AIAssistantSkills/
    ├── ach-mover-movement/
    ├── addressables/
    ├── localization/
    └── ...
```

## Discovery and activation

Skills are discovered when the Editor starts and after a domain reload. To activate them:

1. Open `Edit > Preferences > AI > Skills`.
2. Find the 12 AchEngine entries under **Package skills**.
3. Change each status from `Deny` to `Allow`.
4. Start a new Assistant conversation so it reads the updated skill set.

## What the skills do

They guide the Assistant toward AchEngine's movement, async, ECS, Localization, A\*, Singleton, HttpLink, UI catalog, timer, manager, VContainer, and Addressables APIs.

## Add project-specific skills

Place a project skill under the project's configured AI Assistant skills directory and document its trigger, allowed actions, and the APIs it should prefer.



---
url: /AchEngine/en/usage/mcp/skills.md
---

> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /AchEngine/en/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /AchEngine/en/llms-full.txt.

# Skill List

| Skill                 | Focus                                 |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `ach-mover-movement`  | AchMover movement and collision       |
| `ach-task-async`      | AchTask async operations              |
| `ach-timer`           | AchTimer and UIAchTimer               |
| `addressables`        | AddressableManager and editor tooling |
| `ecs-ingame-logic`    | ECS gameplay logic                    |
| `httplink-webrequest` | HttpLink HTTP requests                |
| `imanager-managers`   | AchEngine managers                    |
| `localization`        | LocalizationManager and locale data   |
| `pathfinding-astar`   | A\* grids and pathfinding             |
| `singleton`           | Singleton base classes                |
| `ui-catalog`          | UIView catalog and UI workspace       |
| `vcontainer-di`       | AchEngine DI and VContainer           |

## Shared rules

- Prefer an existing AchEngine feature instead of recreating it.
- `ecs-ingame-logic` and `vcontainer-di` ask the user before applying architectural changes.
- The authoritative instructions are the `SKILL.md` files under `AIAssistantSkills/<skill-name>`.

# AchMover

`AchMover` is a plug-in 2D character movement component. It does **not** use `Rigidbody2D`; it implements Move-and-Slide collision, gravity, slopes, stairs, and ground snapping directly.

## Usage

Add `AchMover` and a `CapsuleCollider2D` to the character. Drive movement by setting the input or calling the public movement methods from your controller.

## Inspector

### Movement

Configure move speed, acceleration, deceleration, jump speed, and air control.

### Physics

Configure gravity, terminal velocity, skin width, and collision layers.

### Slopes & stairs

Set `MaxSlopeAngle` and `StepHeight` to control walkable slopes and automatic stair climbing.

### Control

Enable or disable gravity and movement, and choose the update mode appropriate for the controller.

## Built-in collision system

Each frame the component:

1. Combines input, gravity, and jump velocity.
2. Casts the capsule and slides along collision surfaces, up to four iterations.
3. Steps over ledges within `StepHeight`.
4. Casts below the collider and marks the character grounded when the surface is within `MaxSlopeAngle`.
5. Snaps to the ground while descending slopes.
6. Corrects any remaining penetration.

## State properties

```csharp
var mover = GetComponent<AchMover>();
bool grounded = mover.IsGrounded;
Vector2 velocity = mover.Velocity;
```

## Joystick or custom input

```csharp
mover.SetMoveInput(new Vector2(horizontal, vertical));
mover.SetJumpPressed();
```

## Code-control API

```csharp
mover.Move(Vector2.right);
mover.Jump();
mover.AddImpulse(new Vector2(3f, 2f));
```

### Knockback

```csharp
private void OnHit(Vector2 direction)
{
    GetComponent<AchMover>().AddImpulse(direction.normalized * 8f);
}
```

## Combining `UseGravity`

Disable `UseGravity` when another system owns vertical movement. Re-enable it before returning control to AchMover.

## `AchFollower` — AI following

`AchFollower` is a standalone target-following component. It does not require `AchMover`.

```csharp
var follower = GetComponent<AchFollower>();
follower.SetTarget(playerTransform);
follower.ClearTarget();
```

## `AchProjectile` — projectiles

`AchProjectile` supports straight and homing projectiles without `Rigidbody2D`. Configure speed, lifetime, collision layers, and the projectile type in the Inspector, then set the target for a homing shot.

```csharp
var projectile = Instantiate(projectilePrefab);
projectile.Launch(direction);
projectile.SetTarget(target);
```

## Trigger and collision events

Use the component's hit/trigger callbacks to apply damage or effects. Keep gameplay response in the listener rather than modifying the movement solver.

# A* Pathfinding

`AStarPathfinder` searches a shortest grid path with A\*. It supports four-way or diagonal eight-way movement and uses a binary min-heap for efficient open-set operations.

## Quick start

### 1. Scan a scene with `AStarGridBaker`

Add _*A* Grid Baker_\* to an empty GameObject, configure the grid size and obstacle layer, and inspect the green walkable/red blocked gizmos in the Scene view.

```csharp
var baker = GetComponent<AStarGridBaker>();
Vector2Int start = baker.WorldToCell(player.position);
Vector2Int end = baker.WorldToCell(targetPosition);

var path = AStarPathfinder.FindPath(baker.Grid, start, end, diagonal: true);
foreach (var cell in path)
{
    Vector3 worldPosition = baker.CellToWorld(cell);
    // Move to the waypoint, for example through AchFollower.
}
```

An unreachable target returns an empty `List<Vector2Int>`.

### Follow a path with `AchFollower`

Use `AchFollower.SetTarget()` for simple following. For waypoints, move through the cells in order and clear the target at the end.

```csharp
var follower = GetComponent<AchFollower>();
foreach (var cell in path)
{
    Vector2 waypoint = baker.CellToWorld(cell);
    follower.SetTarget(waypointTransform);
    while (Vector2.Distance(transform.position, waypoint) > 0.05f)
        await Task.Yield();
}
follower.ClearTarget();
```

### 2. Create a grid in code

```csharp
var grid = new AStarGrid(20, 20);
grid.SetWalkable(5, 3, false);
grid.SetCost(4, 4, 3f);

var path = AStarPathfinder.FindPath(
    grid,
    start: new Vector2Int(0, 0),
    end: new Vector2Int(19, 19),
    diagonal: false);
```

## `AStarGridBaker` settings

| Field              | Description                                                           |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Width` / `Height` | Number of cells                                                       |
| `CellSize`         | Unity-unit size of one cell                                           |
| `Origin`           | Transform for the lower-left cell; empty uses the GameObject position |
| `ObstacleLayer`    | Layers treated as obstacles                                           |
| `DetectionRadius`  | Obstacle radius per cell; `cellSize * 0.4` is a useful starting point |
| `CostZones`        | Collider2D and cost pairs                                             |
| `DrawGizmos`       | Scene-view visualization toggle                                       |

Call `baker.Bake()` after changing dynamic obstacles. Tilemap colliders can be placed on the obstacle layer.

## Grid and pathfinder APIs

```csharp
var grid = new AStarGrid(width: 20, height: 20);
grid.SetWalkable(5, 3, false);
grid.SetCost(4, 4, 3f);
bool walkable = grid.IsWalkable(5, 3);
float cost = grid.GetCost(4, 4);
bool inBounds = grid.IsInBounds(5, 3);

List<Vector2Int> path = AStarPathfinder.FindPath(
    grid, new Vector2Int(0, 0), new Vector2Int(10, 10), diagonal: true);
```

The returned path excludes the start cell and includes the destination. `diagonal` defaults to `false`.

## Algorithm details

| Item          | Detail                                          |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Search        | A\* with a binary min-heap open set             |
| Heuristic     | Manhattan for four-way; Chebyshev for eight-way |
| Diagonal cost | √2 ≈ 1.414                                      |
| Cell weights  | Set with `AStarGrid.SetCost()`                  |
| Complexity    | O((W×H) log(W×H))                               |

Diagonal movement permits corner cutting when the diagonal cell is open. Disable diagonal movement or add an adjacent-cell check if that behavior is undesirable.

# Singleton

## `Singleton<T>` — pure C# singleton

Use the pure C# base for services that do not need a Unity lifecycle.

```csharp
public sealed class GameRules : Singleton<GameRules>
{
    public int MaxPlayers = 4;
}

var rules = GameRules.Instance;
```

## `MonoSingleton<T>` — scene-local singleton

Use this base for a component that should have one instance in the current scene.

```csharp
public class ObjectTouchManager : MonoSingleton<ObjectTouchManager> { }
```

## `PersistentMonoSingleton<T>` — persistent singleton

Use this base when the component should survive scene changes through `DontDestroyOnLoad`.

```csharp
public class AudioRoot : PersistentMonoSingleton<AudioRoot> { }
```

# Code Generation & Runtime

## Generate code

Table Loader generates type-safe C# data classes from CSV.

```text
Id,Name,Price,IsActive
101,Iron Sword,500,TRUE
```

```csharp
[MemoryPackable]
public partial class ItemData : ITableData
{
    public int Id { get; set; }
    public string Name { get; set; }
    public int Price { get; set; }
    public bool IsActive { get; set; }
}

public class ItemTable : ITableDatabase<int, ItemData> { }
```

Click **Generate Code** in the **Table Loader** window or **Project Settings › Table Loader**.

## Bake

Bake the generated data into `.bytes` when MemoryPack is installed, or `.json` otherwise. Files are written below `binaryOutputPath`.


> **Place files under Resources**
> 
> Place baked files under a `Resources/` folder so runtime code can load them with `Resources.Load`, for example `Assets/GameData/Resources/Tables/Item.bytes`.
> 


## Runtime access

```csharp
var itemTable = TableManager.Get<ItemTable>();
var item = itemTable.Get(101);
Debug.Log($"{item.Name}: {item.Price}");

foreach (var row in itemTable.All)
    Debug.Log(row.Name);
```

## Use with DI

```csharp
public class GlobalInstaller : AchEngineInstaller
{
    public override void Install(IServiceBuilder builder)
        => builder.Register<ITableService, TableService>();
}

public class GameService : IGameService
{
    private readonly ITableService _tables;

    public GameService(ITableService tables) => _tables = tables;
}
```

# Table Loader — Overview

Table Loader downloads Google Sheets data, generates C# types, and bakes runtime data.


> **Optional package**
> 
> `com.cysharp.memorypack` is optional. When installed, baked data uses `.bytes`; otherwise it uses JSON.
> 


## Pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart LR
A[Google Sheets] --> B[Download CSV]
B --> C[Generate C#]
C --> D[Bake data]
D --> E[Resources]
E --> F[TableManager]
```

## Main settings

| Setting             | Description                                    |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| Spreadsheet ID      | ID from the Google Sheets URL                  |
| CSV output path     | Download destination                           |
| Generated code path | C# output destination                          |
| Binary output path  | `.bytes` or `.json` destination                |
| Sheet list          | Sheet name, GID, and generated class name      |
| Automation          | Generate and bake automatically after download |

## Next steps

- [Settings & download](/AchEngine/en/usage/table/setup.md)
- [JSON → CSV export](/AchEngine/en/usage/table/json-to-csv.md)
- [Code generation & runtime](/AchEngine/en/usage/table/codegen.md)

url: /AchEngine/en/usage/table/json-to-csv.md

> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /AchEngine/en/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /AchEngine/en/llms-full.txt.

# JSON → CSV Export

## Open the tool

Open **AchEngine › Table JSON to CSV** from the Unity Editor.

## Supported JSON

The importer accepts an array of objects:

```json
[
  { "Id": 101, "Name": "Iron Sword", "Price": 500 },
  { "Id": 102, "Name": "Magic Wand", "Price": 1200 }
]
```

It also accepts a wrapper object whose data is stored in a property such as `items`:

```json
{
  "items": [
    { "Id": 101, "Name": "Iron Sword" }
  ]
}
```

## CSV output

```csv
Id,Name,Price
101,Iron Sword,500
102,Magic Wand,1200
```

## Convert one file

1. Choose a `.json` file with **Select JSON**.
2. Choose the output `.csv` path with **Select CSV Location**.
3. Click **Convert File**.

## Convert a folder

1. Choose the input folder with **Select JSON Folder**.
2. Choose the output folder with **Select CSV Folder**.
3. Enable **Include Subfolders** to recurse into child folders.
4. Click **Convert Folder**.

url: /AchEngine/en/usage/table/setup.md

> For AI agents: the complete documentation index is available at /AchEngine/en/llms.txt, the full documentation bundle is available at /AchEngine/en/llms-full.txt.

# Settings & Download

## Initial setup

Open **Project Settings › AchEngine › Table Loader** and:

1. Enter the **Spreadsheet ID**.
2. Set CSV, code, and binary output paths.
3. Add sheets with a sheet name, GID, and class name.
4. Click **Save Settings**.

Settings are stored in `Assets/TableLoaderSettings.asset`.

## Prepare Google Sheets

1. Set the sheet sharing option to **Anyone with the link → Viewer**.
2. Copy the ID from `https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/[SPREADSHEET_ID]/edit`.
3. Copy each sheet's `gid=` value from its URL.

## Sheet data format

The first row is the C# property names and the following rows are data.

```text
| Id  | Name       | Price | IsActive |
|-----|------------|-------|----------|
| 101 | Iron Sword | 500   | TRUE     |
| 102 | Magic Wand | 1200  | TRUE     |
```


> **Supported types**
> 
> `int`, `float`, `bool`, `string`, and `long` are supported. A column named `Id` is used as the default key.
> 


## Register sheets

| Field      | Description                  |
| ---------- | ---------------------------- |
| Enabled    | Whether to process the sheet |
| Sheet Name | Google Sheets tab name       |
| GID        | Sheet ID from the URL        |
| Class Name | Generated C# class name      |

## Download CSV

Click **Open Table Loader** or use **Tools › AchEngine › Table Loader**, then click **Download CSV**. Files are created under `csvOutputPath`.

## Automation

Enable automatic code generation after download and automatic baking after code generation to run **Download → Generate → Bake** in one click.

## JSON → CSV

Use **AchEngine › Table JSON to CSV** to convert baked JSON back to Google Sheets-compatible CSV. See [JSON → CSV export](/AchEngine/en/usage/table/json-to-csv.md).
